content.value_statement: Google Meet records and spaces can be difficult to inspect consistently from a terminal. This skill guides structured discovery and management through the gws CLI.
actual_capabilities: Get a conference record by conference ID.
List conference records ordered by start time.
Discover operations for participants, recordings, smart notes, and transcripts.
Create, retrieve, and update Google Meet spaces.
End an active conference in a meeting space.
Inspect method schemas before constructing parameters and request data.
limitations: The gws CLI and its shared authentication skill must be available.
Google Workspace permissions and API access determine which operations succeed.
The skill lists nested resources but does not document every nested method.
Destructive or sensitive operations still require user review.

use_cases.title: Review Recent Meetings
use_cases.description: List recent conference records and retrieve details for a selected conference.

use_cases.title: Inspect Meeting Artifacts
use_cases.description: Discover available participant, recording, smart note, and transcript operations for a conference.

use_cases.title: Manage Meeting Spaces
use_cases.description: Create, inspect, update, or end conferences in managed meeting spaces.

prompt_templates.title: List Conferences
prompt_templates.prompt: List my recent Google Meet conference records. Inspect the method schema first, then summarize the returned meetings by start time.

prompt_templates.title: Get Conference Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the Google Meet conference record with ID [conference ID]. Inspect required parameters first and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Conference Artifacts
prompt_templates.prompt: For conference [conference ID], inspect available methods for participants, recordings, smart notes, and transcripts. Explain which operations match my access.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Meeting Space
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the patch schema for meeting space [space name]. Propose parameters for [requested change], show the planned update, and wait for confirmation.

output_examples.input: List recent Google Meet conference records.
output: Three conference records were returned in descending start-time order.
The latest record started at 14:00 UTC and includes participant and transcript resources.
Select a conference ID to retrieve full details.

output_examples.output: The meeting space was found. An active conference is present, and the current space settings are available for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare an update to the meeting space.
output_examples.output: The patch schema was inspected. The proposed fields are ready for review, and no update has been sent.

best_practices: Inspect each method schema before supplying parameters or request data.
Confirm conference and space identifiers before running an operation.
Request explicit approval before updates or ending an active conference.
anti_patterns: Do not guess parameter names or request shapes.
Do not expose participant, transcript, or recording data beyond authorized users.
Do not end an active conference without clear user confirmation.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The gws CLI must be available, and the shared gws authentication instructions must be configured.

faq.question: Can this skill list past conferences?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use the conferenceRecords list method and summarize records returned by your account.

faq.question: Can it retrieve participants and transcripts?
faq.answer: It can discover and use supported operations for participants and transcripts when your account has permission.

faq.question: Can it create a meeting space?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented spaces resource includes a create method.

faq.question: Can it end an active conference?
faq.answer: Yes. The spaces resource includes endActiveConference, but the action should require explicit confirmation.

faq.question: How are method parameters determined?
faq.answer: The skill uses gws schema output to inspect required parameters, types, defaults, and request fields.
